context.clinical_context_summary: 82-year-old male with a past medical history of recurrent urinary issues (UTI, urinary retention/BPH), orthostatic hypotension, lymphedema/varicose veins, diabetes (on metformin), hypothyroidism (on levothyroxine), prior severe sepsis/bacteremia and hypotension, and prior melena, on midodrine, tamsulosin, furosemide, metformin ER, levothyroxine, dabigatran, and TMP-SMX among others. Presents with generalized weakness. Recent temperatures are consistently febrile (mean 38.1°C, max 39.7°C), which is concerning for infection/sepsis given history; TMP-SMX use may indicate active/treated infection. Baseline blood pressures trend low (mean SBP ~94) consistent with orthostatic hypotension and midodrine use; even “normal” pressures for him may be lower than standard and he is at risk for shock with further drops. Anticoagulated (dabigatran) with history of melena → elevated bleeding risk, especially if hypotensive or anemic; diuretic use increases dehydration/electrolyte risk.
context.rationale: Thresholds were personalized to his observed baseline: SBP averages in the mid-90s with known orthostatic hypotension on midodrine, so the normal SBP range is shifted lower while keeping conservative warning/critical cutoffs for shock. HR is centered around his mean (~73) with broader warnings to detect brady/tachyarrhythmia in an older patient. SpO2 is set to standard safety ranges because his baseline is normal (94–100%). RR is kept near standard with a slightly higher upper-normal to reflect his mean (~21) while flagging ≥27 as abnormal. Temperature is treated as core/oral given consistently high values (37.7–39.7°C); thus >38.0°C is a warning and >39.0°C would be high concern for sepsis in this context.
